title: Brass bands and first road trip with a circus band
summary: He toured with an outfit from St. Louis, was stranded, led a circus orchestra with trumpeter P.G. Lowry, and went to New York.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Do you remember any other real early music when you were abroad? When you were a boy, did they have any of the street parades? You know, they have now a lot of the parades. They even use them for funerals and- Oh, gosh, yes.
They had the brass bands when you were a boy. Uh-huh.

You know, because I had a taste of that myself after I began running around the country. That was one of my first trips. I went away with an outfit that was organized in St. Louis. And, uh, we traveled around the country for a while and had the misfortune of being stranded. And from there, we- I lined up with, uh, a very famous trumpet player we had by the- who was, at that time, with the Four Point Ring Brothers Circus. His name was P.G. Lowry.

Very, very, very famous trumpet. Well, he was the bandmaster and he heard me play and asked me if I would take the orchestra. And we left St. Louis with that outfit and went to New York, the old Madison Square Garden. And, uh, we rehearsed there for a couple of weeks before we went on the road. And then we went on the road and I stayed out with that outfit, oh, about two years. Then went back to New Orleans, stayed in New Orleans, and of course the old man got after me for about- but running around the country. And I stayed home for a while, but the bug had stuck me. So I had an opportunity to leave and I left and came to Chicago.
